title: Thyroid antibodies (anti-TPO)
what: This is a blood test from a vein. It looks for antibodies that can attack your thyroid gland.
why: For changes in thyroid hormones, an enlarged thyroid, when planning a pregnancy, or for infertility.
duration: the blood draw takes a few minutes; results usually come in 1 to 3 days
tell_doctor: If you take thyroid hormones or iodine
If you take biotin or vitamins with biotin
If you are pregnant or planning a pregnancy

prepare.title: Food
prepare.text: Strict fasting is usually not needed. But it is best in the morning before eating, or 3 to 4 hours after a light meal. Check with the lab.

prepare.title: The day before
prepare.text: For 24 hours, no alcohol and no hard workouts. Best not to smoke in the morning.

prepare.title: Medicines
prepare.text: Do not stop them on your own. Tell your doctor what you take. They will decide if anything should change.

bring: Past thyroid hormone tests and thyroid ultrasound, if you have them
steps: You sit down and rest your arm on the armrest
A band is tightened above your elbow
The skin is wiped with antiseptic
A quick prick, and blood fills a tube
The needle comes out, and a cotton pad is pressed on the spot
feel: A quick prick, like a pinch
Sometimes slight dizziness. Tell the nurse
after: Press the cotton pad for 3 to 5 minutes and keep your arm straight
You can eat right away and go back to your usual day
Results usually come in 1 to 3 days. The lab will tell you when

faq.q: Do high antibodies mean I am ill?
faq.a: Not always. Many people have high antibodies and normal hormones. Your doctor looks at all the tests together.

faq.q: Do I need to repeat anti-TPO often?
faq.a: Usually not. Your doctor will tell you how often.

reminders.text: Thyroid antibody test tomorrow. Best to come before eating. Water is fine.
